questions.question: What is a Rube Goldberg Machine in physics game design?
options: A complex chain-reaction machine where one physics action triggers another to achieve a simple goal
questions.explanation: Correct! Rube Goldberg machines utilize chain-reaction physics (e.g. ball hits dominos, domino pushes lever).

questions.question: If you want to create multiple identical balls in your Rube Goldberg machine without making new sprites, what block should you use?
questions.explanation: Excellent! Cloning generates duplicate active physical balls dynamically during runtime.

questions.question: In a 3D Car Simulator game, which block is used to steer the tires and drive the car around corners?
questions.explanation: Perfect! The 'steer car' block angles the wheels, turning the chassis as it drives forward.

questions.question: How can we make a camera follow closely behind our 3D car as it moves through the city?
options: Place a point light in the car
Attach the camera to the target car sprite using follow offset blocks
questions.explanation: Spot on! Attaching the camera lock-follow offset to the car keeps the player in the center of view while driving.

questions.question: What makes a 3D car's tires grip the road and steer effectively without spinning out of control?
options: Physical friction between the wheels and the street surface
questions.explanation: Great! Friction provides traction, letting tires push against the asphalt to turn.

questions.question: If a ball slides off the edge of a Rube Goldberg slope, why does it travel in a downward curve?
options: Due to the combined forward speed force and downward pull of gravity physics
questions.explanation: Perfect! Gravity pulls it down while its horizontal inertia keeps it moving forward, creating a realistic curve!

questions.question: Which physical body shape is ideal for a spherical rolling marble inside a track?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The 'sphere' shape is optimized for round objects, ensuring smooth roll physics.

questions.question: Why do we sometimes need to adjust and fine-tune physical coordinates of dominoes in a Goldberg chain?
options: To ensure they align perfectly so the falling ball strikes them centered, triggering the fall
questions.explanation: Great! Alignment troubleshooting is key in physics to ensure chain-reactions don't miss or break.

questions.question: What blocks drawer contains physical templates and body settings in PicToBlox 3D?
questions.explanation: Perfect! The 'Physics 3D' extension drawer houses all blocks for gravity, mass, force, and bounce settings.

questions.question: What block removes a physical ball clone once it falls off the bottom screen to save memory?
questions.explanation: Perfect! 'delete this clone' removes the finished sprite clone, preventing resource leaks.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to drive a 3D car sprite forward at speed 15 and steer it at a 30-degree angle when the Right Arrow key is pressed.
questions.task_hint: when right arrow key pressed -> move car speed(15) -> steer car angle(30)
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Connecting keypress triggers to speed and steering enables interactive driving!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to delete a ball clone when its Y-coordinate drops below -300.
questions.task_hint: if y position < -300 then delete this clone
questions.explanation: Perfect! Discarding falling items maintains smooth physics gameplay!
